items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Oscar Goodstein, one of them, said, “Bird, you can’t come in here.”

ctx.x: He fell off. Brown, C.: Was he in pain?

Yeah. He got up and got back up and played. I mean, he was famous for dancing around like that and, you know. Oh, my God. But I didn‟t know Monk the way I knew Bird, you know. And, and one of the tragedies with Charlie Parker toward the end of his life was, he would always come by when he felt whatever, and I always felt, here was my hero, and I always felt so honored that he would come by to see if I was okay. And sometimes he‟d make up excuses „cause he couldn‟t go home. And he‟d say, “Oh, I saw the fire trucks…
